newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes up, gas oil ends weaker with heat.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes up, gas oil ends weaker with heat.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed firmer on Tuesday but off highs as a wave of short-covering waned towards the close, while gas oil remained under pressure, brokers said.
April Brent closed five cents up at $20.40 a barrel, having touched a session high in late afternoon dealing of $20.62.
Brent trading closed early at 1730 GMT because of an Institute of Petroleum Week function.
"We had a short-covering rally fuelled by the strength in (NYMEX crude)," said one dealer.
Brokers said the dip towards the close was due to selling by one big player.
Brent had earlier dipped to a session low of $20.10, the lowest level for the prompt contract since August 28, in a follow-through to Monday's sell-off.
Traders said they saw support for Brent at the psychological level of $22.00 a barrel, and also at $19.96, the lowest level reached in last week's sell-off.
March gas oil failed to retrace losses, however, ending the session at six month lows of $174.75, $2.50 down on the day and 50 cents off the day's low.
Brokers said that weak NYMEX heating oil stopped gas oil from following Brent higher.
"The heat ticked up a bit, but it's still under pressure," said one.
March heating oil shed over two cents a gallon on forecasts of mild U.S. temperatures in early trade before recovering to trade 0.91 cents down at 59.90 cents a gallon at 1756 GMT.
Weekly U.S. stocks data which is usually released after the close of trade on Tuesday is expected to be delayed by 24 hours because of a national holiday in the U.S. on Monday.
